story: William Carey defeated Andrew College 6-0 at Danny Owens Field in Hattiesburg on Monday. The result completed Carey's men's soccer regular season. Pedro Sao Tiago opened the scoring in the 13th minute after a saved shot. Jean Danitanga increased the advantage in the 39th minute. Carey led 2-0 at halftime, before adding four goals in the second half. Daniel Mulero scored in the 77th minute from an Isaiah Harvey cross.

Blue Mountain Christian won its women's basketball season opener against Tougaloo, 67-62, at Kroger Gym. BMCU led 35-32 at halftime and 50-45 after three quarters. Channing Lane scored 18 points from the bench on 7-of-10 shooting. Lena Taylor contributed 15 points, eight rebounds and four steals. McKenzie Williams had 11 points and 11 rebounds. Isabella Aversa scored 10 points. The Toppers recorded 44 rebounds and 12 steals. The team made 23 of its 56 field-goal attempts.

Delta State running back Nick Clark received the Gulf South Conference offensive player of the week honor. Qualon Farrar had received the same award the previous week. Clark ran for 178 yards and a touchdown in a 37-33 victory over West Alabama. Through seven games his totals were 500 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. During the four-game winning streak he averaged 119.5 rushing yards per game. The next opponent was Frostburg State.

Southern Virginia defeated Belhaven 23-19 at Belhaven Bowl Stadium. Jalen Lackey caught Rylen Balser's 37-yard touchdown pass with 46 seconds left. Belhaven had led 19-8 entering the fourth quarter, before Southern Virginia scored the last 15 points. Both teams finished the game with records of 3-4 overall and 2-2 in the USA South. Belhaven's next opponent was Methodist. Matthew Dial completed 13 of 23 passes for 147 yards and a touchdown. Ian Burleson completed all three attempts for 69 yards and a score. Nehemiah Philip caught four passes for 87 yards. Johnathan Lampkin also had four catches, gaining 76 yards with a touchdown. John Ross Craven led the Belhaven defense with 11 tackles. Jimmy Byrd made 10 tackles, including three for loss and two sacks. Belhaven's defense recorded seven sacks and 10 tackles for loss. Southern Virginia gained 411 yards, compared with Belhaven's 227. Lackey had 11 receptions for 215 yards and two touchdowns. Seven sacks by Southern Virginia left Belhaven with 11 net rushing yards. The crowd numbered 2,478. Belhaven reached Southern Virginia's 32 on its final possession but the final pass was incomplete. The Knights had recovered a fumble after a Belhaven interception to begin their winning drive.

Hinds defeated Northwest Mississippi 2-1 in men's soccer on October 23. D'neit Chambers scored both Hinds goals. The teams were level at halftime without a goal. Chambers scored in the 49th minute, putting Hinds ahead. Osvaldo Macias equalized from Joseph Jackson's corner kick in the 80th minute. Chambers then beat the goalkeeper in a one-on-one opportunity in the 84th minute. The second goal restored a lead Hinds kept until the final whistle. Chambers attempted four shots, with two on target. Juan Paredas-Montaño took two shots. Nicholas Baker attempted two shots, and Quade Hollingsworth had three. Bray Wilson played all 90 minutes in goal, recording four saves and allowing one goal. Hinds was scheduled to face Jones College on October 27 at Tom Shepherd Field, with kickoff at 4 PM.

Reagan Shinn received The W's Owl of the Week award for October 19-25. The women's soccer player scored her seventh goal of the season in a 3-2 loss to Westminster. The goal put Shinn among the conference's top 10 scorers. Her season total tied for third in MUW history, with one match left.
